findings.where: "Where we're starting" section: the Canggu, Uluwatu and Kuta Lombok destination cards, each with its "Best hostels" line and chevron
findings.fault: The cards look clickable, but nothing on them is a link. Each is a white raised card with a hover style. It has a heavy coloured border and a shadow, and its "Best hostels" line is in link colour with a chevron. The parts map lists all three as static, and none goes to a guide. Sending visitors to the destination guides is one of this page's three jobs, and these cards are the only route to the guides.
findings.who_objects: The backpacker on a phone who taps "Canggu · Best hostels" to see where to stay and gets no response. They can't reach a guide from here and will think the site is broken or empty before launch. The founder would object too: the guides are the page's SEO payoff, and this page leads nowhere into them.

findings.where: Top nav "How we rank" link and footer "How we rank" link
findings.fault: "How we rank" links back to this same page, so it is a dead link. The page has no ranking-method section to land on. Merit-only ranking is the claim the hero makes, and this link offers the evidence for it, then does nothing.
findings.who_objects: The visitor who reads "ranks Indonesia's hostels on merit alone", has doubts and clicks to check. They get nothing back, and the claim now looks empty. The product principle "rankings and scoring methods are published" breaks right at the place the page invites the check.

findings.where: Footer links: Privacy, Terms, Report content
findings.fault: All three link back to this same page, so they are dead. The page is asking visitors for their email address while its Privacy link leads nowhere.
findings.who_objects: A careful visitor who looks for the privacy terms before sending their address, and anyone who wants to report content. Each finds a link that does nothing, which reads as a placeholder site.

findings.where: Hero primary action: the coral "Email luc@mantahostels.com for launch news" button
findings.fault: The page's main action is a plain mailto link. It has no subject line and no sign-up step. On a desktop with no mail app set up, the click does nothing visible. Where a mail app does open, the visitor gets a blank email and has to work out what to write to be added to the list.
findings.who_objects: A visitor who wants launch news and clicks the biggest button on the page. They get no response, or an empty email to compose, and many will give up. That loses the contacts this page exists to collect.

findings.fault: The two nav links look different. "How we rank" is underlined and "Destinations" is not. The underline suggests "How we rank" is the current page or a different kind of link, but both are the same kind of nav link.
findings.who_objects: A visitor scanning the nav may take "How we rank" for the page they are already on, or treat "Destinations" as not a link. Either way the nav sends a mixed signal.
